title: Through the heavens
hookLine: he rises through the heavens, meeting Adam, Isa, Yahya, Yusuf, Idris, Harun, Musa and Ibrahim (Bukhari)

cards: A gate in the sky, and a voice behind it asking: who is it? Jibril. And who is with you?
Muhammad. Has he been sent for? Yes.
Then welcome to him; what an excellent visit. And the gate opens. In Sahih al-Bukhari, that short exchange happens again and again, at gate after gate.
Muslims tell it as the same night as yesterday's journey: Jerusalem was the first leg. Now he rises. Today's word: Mi'raj, the ascent.

teach.b: Mi'raj is the name Muslims give to the ascent. Bukhari's reports, from Malik ibn Sa'sa'a and others, walk through it heaven by heaven, and at each one, someone is waiting. In the first heaven, Adam.
Another report in Bukhari, from Abu Dharr, describes figures to his right and to his left: when he looks to the right he laughs, and when he looks to the left he weeps.
They are his own descendants, the people of the garden on one side, the people of the fire on the other.
In the second heaven, two cousins, Yahya and Isa, John and Jesus. In the third, Yusuf. In the fourth, Idris.
In the fifth, Harun, the brother of Musa. In the sixth, Musa himself. And in the seventh, Ibrahim.
At each heaven the greeting is nearly the same. Adam and Ibrahim say: welcome, righteous son, righteous prophet.
The others say: welcome, righteous brother, righteous prophet. Son, from the fathers. Brother, from the rest.
A few days ago, three brothers in Ta'if wouldn't even speak to him.
Now every heaven has family in it. Beyond the seventh heaven, the reports describe the lote tree of the furthest boundary, which the Qur'an mentions in surah fifty-three.
The Qur'an itself gives few details of the ascent; the details are in the hadith. Some of these names appear in the Bible too, as Adam, John, Jesus, Joseph, Aaron, Moses and Abraham.
Here they stand at their stations, waiting to say welcome.

how: Muslims learn the order of the heavens and the prophets met in each from the hadith of the Mi'raj, and say 'peace be upon him' after a prophet's name.

o: the lote tree at the boundary

s: the Qur'an gives the full list of heavens and prophets
those details are in the hadith; the Qur'an gives few details of the ascent.
Adam and Ibrahim greet him as a son
the others greet him as a brother.
at each gate the gatekeeper questions the Prophet himself
the questions go to Jibril, who answers: Muhammad.

games.q: in the first heaven you see Adam with figures to his right and left. when he looks to the left, what does he do?
games.why: Abu Dharr's report in Bukhari: he laughs looking right and weeps looking left; both sides are his descendants.

practice: If you can, look at the sky through a window or outside; if not, close your eyes and picture it.
Then name them in order, one per breath, Adam, Yahya and Isa, Yusuf, Idris, Harun, Musa, Ibrahim, letting one thing you remember about each come up.
If you pray, you can send peace on each of them, as Muslims do when they say the prophets' names.

wordCard.voice: Mi'raj: the ascent. In Bukhari, he rises through the heavens and at each one a prophet greets him, as a son or as a brother. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the ascent; the name given to this part of the night journey.

carryVoice: Your line: met at every heaven. Turned away below, welcomed above. Day seven hundred fifty-five, done.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 3207 (Malik ibn Sa'sa'a: the gates, 'who is it? has he been sent for?'; Adam, Yahya and Isa, Yusuf, Idris, Harun, Musa, Ibrahim; the greetings)
Sahih al-Bukhari 349 (Abu Dharr: Adam laughs looking right, weeps looking left)
Qur'an 53:13–16 (the lote tree of the furthest boundary)
